title.zh: 卷五十六 志第四十六 刑法
title.raw: 卷五十六 志第四十六 刑法 Volume 56 Treatises 52: Punishment and Law

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 古之為國者，議事以制，不為刑辟，懼民之知爭端也。

translations.literal: In antiquity those who governed states deliberated affairs to establish norms and did not create criminal statutes, fearing that the people would learn the points of contention.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, rulers governed by deliberating affairs and setting norms rather than drafting criminal codes, because they feared teaching the people where disputes might arise.

sentences.zh: 後世作為刑書，惟恐不備，俾民之知所避也。

translations.literal: Later ages composed books of criminal law, fearing only that they might not be complete, so as to enable the people to know what to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations wrote penal codes and worried chiefly that nothing be left out, so that the people might know what to shun.

sentences.zh: 其為法雖殊，而用心則一，蓋皆欲民之無犯也。

translations.literal: Although the making of law differed, the intent was one: all wished that the people should not offend.
translations.idiomatic: The methods differed, but the aim was the same: both approaches sought to keep the people from breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 然未知夫導之以德、齊之以禮，而可使民遷善遠罪而不自知也。

translations.literal: Yet they did not know that by guiding them with virtue and regulating them with ritual, one could cause the people to turn toward goodness and away from crime without their being aware of it.
translations.idiomatic: They did not yet grasp that guiding people with virtue and harmonizing them through ritual could move them toward goodness and away from crime before they even realized it.

sentences.zh: 唐之刑書有四，曰：律、令、格、式。

translations.literal: The Tang had four books of criminal law, called: Statutes, Ordinances, Administrative Precedents, and Formulae.
translations.idiomatic: Tang criminal law comprised four bodies of text: the Statutes, the Ordinances, the Administrative Precedents, and the Formulae.

sentences.zh: 令者，尊卑貴賤之等數，國家之制度也；

translations.literal: Ordinances were the gradations of noble and base, exalted and humble, and the institutions of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinances defined the ranks of high and low and the institutions of the realm.

sentences.zh: 格者，百官有司之所常行之事也；

translations.literal: Administrative Precedents were the matters that the hundred officials and their departments regularly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Precedents recorded the routine duties of the hundred officials and their bureaus.

sentences.zh: 式者，其所常守之法也。

translations.literal: Formulae were the laws that they regularly observed.
translations.idiomatic: Formulae set out the standard procedures they were to follow.

sentences.zh: 凡邦國之政，必從事於此三者。

translations.literal: In all the affairs of the state, one had necessarily to attend to these three.
translations.idiomatic: All governance of the realm had to proceed through these three categories.

sentences.zh: 其有所違及人之為惡而入于罪戾者，一斷以律。

translations.literal: Where there was violation of them, or where men did evil and fell into guilt, all was adjudicated by the Statutes alone.
translations.idiomatic: Any breach of them, or any act of malice that brought a person within the scope of punishment, was resolved solely under the Statutes.

sentences.zh: 律之為書，因隋之舊，為十有二篇：一曰名例，二曰衞禁，三曰職制，四曰戶婚，五曰廄庫，六曰擅興，七曰賊盜，八曰鬬訟，九曰詐偽，十曰雜律，十一曰捕亡，十二曰斷獄。

translations.literal: The book of Statutes followed the Sui precedent and had twelve sections: first, General Principles; second, Frontier Security and Prohibitions; third, Official Duties and Regulations; fourth, Households and Marriage; fifth, Stables and Storehouses; sixth, Unauthorized Mobilization; seventh, Banditry and Theft; eighth, Assault and Litigation; ninth, Fraud and Forgery; tenth, Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh, Apprehension of Fugitives; twelfth, Trial and Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Statutes followed the Sui model in twelve chapters: General Principles; Frontier Security and Prohibitions; Official Duties and Regulations; Households and Marriage; Stables and Storehouses; Unauthorized Mobilization; Banditry and Theft; Assault and Litigation; Fraud and Forgery; Miscellaneous Statutes; Apprehension of Fugitives; and Trial and Punishment.

sentences.zh: 其用刑有五：一曰笞。

translations.literal: The punishments employed were five: first, beating with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Five punishments were applied: the first was beating with the rod.

sentences.zh: 笞之為言恥也；

translations.literal: The word for rod-beating means shame.
translations.idiomatic: The term for rod-beating denotes shame.

sentences.zh: 凡過之小者，捶撻以恥之。

translations.literal: For all minor offenses, one flogged and beat to shame them.
translations.idiomatic: Minor offenses were punished with flogging meant to humiliate the offender.

sentences.zh: 漢用竹，後世更以楚。

translations.literal: The Han used bamboo; later ages changed to the birch.
translations.idiomatic: The Han used bamboo rods; later dynasties switched to birch switches.

sentences.zh: 書曰「扑作教刑」是也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Documents says, "Flogging serves as corrective punishment" — this is that.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Book of Documents means by "flogging serves as corrective punishment."

sentences.zh: 二曰杖。

translations.literal: Second, the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The second was the staff.

sentences.zh: 杖者，持也：可持以擊也。

translations.literal: The staff means to hold: it can be held to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Staff means "to hold" — something one can grasp to strike with.

sentences.zh: 書曰「鞭作官刑」是也。

translations.literal: The Classic says, "The whip serves as official punishment" — this is that.
translations.idiomatic: This corresponds to the Book of Documents line, "the whip serves as official punishment."

sentences.zh: 三曰徒。

translations.literal: Third, penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The third was penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 徒者，奴也；

translations.literal: Penal servitude means to be a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Servitude meant enslavement.

sentences.zh: 蓋奴辱之。

translations.literal: It was essentially to enslave and humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: It reduced offenders to servile humiliation.

sentences.zh: 周禮曰：其奴，男子入于罪隸，任之以事，寘之圜土而教之，量其罪之輕重，有年數而捨。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say: when they were enslaved, men entered the criminal bondsmen; tasks were assigned to them; they were placed in the Round Mound and instructed; according to the lightness or heaviness of the crime, after a number of years they were released.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou state that male offenders became criminal bondsmen, were put to labor, confined in the Round Mound for instruction, and released after a term set according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 四曰流。

translations.literal: Fourth, exile.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was exile.

sentences.zh: 書云「流宥五刑」，謂不忍刑殺，宥之于遠也。

translations.literal: The Classic says, "Exile pardons the five punishments," meaning that one could not bear to punish by killing and pardoned them in the distance.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, "exile pardons the five punishments," meaning that when execution was too harsh to bear, the offender was spared by banishment to a distant place.

sentences.zh: 五曰死。

translations.literal: Fifth, death.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth was death.

sentences.zh: 乃古大辟之刑也。

translations.literal: This was the ancient punishment of the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ancient capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 自隋以前，死刑有五，曰：罄、絞、斬、梟、裂。

translations.literal: Before the Sui, capital punishment had five forms, called: exposure of the corpse, strangulation, decapitation, display of the severed head, and dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Sui, five forms of capital punishment were recognized: exposure of the corpse, strangulation, decapitation, display of the severed head, and dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 而流、徒之刑，鞭笞兼用，數皆踰百。

translations.literal: As for exile and penal servitude, the whip and the rod were used together, and the counts all exceeded one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and penal servitude were often combined with flogging and rod-beating, with stroke counts sometimes exceeding one hundred.

sentences.zh: 至隋始定為：笞刑五，自十至于五十；

translations.literal: It was only in the Sui that they were first fixed as: five grades of rod-beating, from ten to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui first standardized five grades of rod-beating, ranging from ten to fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 杖刑五，自六十至于百；

translations.literal: Five grades of staff punishment, from sixty to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of staff punishment, from sixty to one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒刑五，自一年至于三年；

translations.literal: Five grades of penal servitude, from one year to three years.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of penal servitude, from one to three years.

sentences.zh: 流刑三，自一千里至于二千里；

translations.literal: Three grades of exile, from one thousand li to two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Three grades of exile, from one thousand to two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 死刑二，絞、斬。

translations.literal: Two forms of capital punishment: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Two forms of capital punishment: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 除其鞭刑及梟首、轘裂之酷。

translations.literal: They abolished the whip punishment and the cruelties of displaying the severed head and cart-sundering.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui abolished flogging with the whip and the cruel punishments of displaying severed heads and cart-sundering.

sentences.zh: 又有議、請、減、贖、當、免之法。

translations.literal: There were also the methods of deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, offset, and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: They also established procedures for deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, offset, and exemption.

sentences.zh: 唐皆因之。

translations.literal: The Tang all followed these.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang adopted all of these provisions.

sentences.zh: 然隋文帝性刻深，而煬帝昏亂，民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wen of Sui was by nature harsh and deep, and Emperor Yang was benighted and chaotic, and the people could not endure their poison.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wen of Sui was harsh by nature, and Emperor Yang was corrupt and erratic, so the people could not endure their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 唐興，高祖入京師，約法十二條，惟殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛逆者死。

translations.literal: When the Tang arose, Gaozu entered the capital and made a compact law of twelve articles; only for murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion was death imposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose, Gaozu entered the capital and proclaimed a twelve-article compact law: only murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion were capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，命納言劉文靜等損益律令。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered the Counselor-in-chief Liu Wenjing and others to add to and subtract from the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the abdication, he ordered Counselor-in-chief Liu Wenjing and others to revise the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，頒新格五十三條，唯吏受賕、犯盜、詐冒府庫物，赦不原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, he promulgated fifty-three new administrative precedents; only for officials receiving bribes, committing theft, or fraudulently claiming goods from the government storehouses was amnesty not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude, he issued fifty-three new administrative precedents, with amnesty withheld only for officials who took bribes, committed theft, or fraudulently claimed government storehouse goods.

sentences.zh: 凡斷屠日及正月、五月、九月不行刑。

translations.literal: On all days when slaughter was forbidden, and in the first, fifth, and ninth months, punishments were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were suspended on slaughter-prohibition days and during the first, fifth, and ninth months.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖躬錄囚徒，以人因亂冒法者眾，盜非劫傷其主及征人逃亡、官吏枉法，皆原之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners; because many people in the turmoil had offended against the law, for theft that did not involve robbery injuring the owner, for conscripts who fled, and for officials who perverted the law, all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the chaos, he pardoned theft without robbery injuring the owner, desertion by conscripts, and official malfeasance.

sentences.zh: 已而又詔僕射裴寂等十五人更撰律令，凡律五百，麗以五十三條。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again ordered the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Ji and fifteen others to compile the statutes and ordinances anew; the statutes totaled five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and fourteen others to draft new statutes and ordinances: five hundred statutory articles supplemented by fifty-three additional provisions.

sentences.zh: 流罪三，皆加千里；

translations.literal: The three grades of exile were all increased by one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: All three grades of exile were increased by one thousand li.

sentences.zh: 居作三歲至二歲半者悉為一歲。

translations.literal: Terms of labor service ranging from three years to two and a half years were all made one year.
translations.idiomatic: Terms of labor service between three years and two and a half years were all reduced to one year.

sentences.zh: 餘無改焉。

translations.literal: In the rest there was no change.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔長孫无忌、房玄齡等復定舊令，議絞刑之屬五十，皆免死而斷右趾。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to fix the old ordinances again; it was proposed that the fifty offenses punishable by strangulation should all escape death and instead have the right foot cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, he ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to revise the old ordinances. They proposed that the fifty offenses punishable by strangulation should be commuted from death to amputation of the right foot.

sentences.zh: 既而又哀其斷毀支體，謂侍臣曰：「肉刑，前代除之久矣，今復斷人趾，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Then again he pitied the cutting and ruin of the limbs and said to his attending ministers: "Corporal punishments were abolished by former ages long ago; now to cut off men's toes again — I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon grew troubled by the mutilation involved and told his ministers, "Corporal punishments were abolished long ago. To cut off men's toes again — I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」王珪、蕭瑀、陳叔達對曰：「受刑者當死而獲生，豈憚去一趾？

translations.literal: " Wang Gui, Xiao Yu, and Chen Shuda replied: "Those who receive punishment would have died but gain life — would they shrink from losing one toe?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Gui, Xiao Yu, and Chen Shuda replied, "Offenders who would have died are allowed to live — would they hesitate to lose a toe?

sentences.zh: 去趾，所以使見者知懼。

translations.literal: Removing the toe is to make those who see it know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Amputation of the toe is meant to instill fear in those who witness it.

sentences.zh: 今以死刑為斷趾，蓋寬之也。

translations.literal: Now to substitute amputation of the toe for the death penalty is essentially to leniently treat them.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing execution with toe amputation is in fact a lenient measure.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公等更思之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You gentlemen, reconsider it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Think it over again.

sentences.zh: 」其後蜀王法曹參軍裴弘獻駮律令四十餘事，乃詔房玄齡與弘獻等重加刪定。

translations.literal: " Later the Legal Bureau aide of the Prince of Shu, Pei Hongxian, submitted objections to more than forty matters in the statutes and ordinances, whereupon an edict ordered Fang Xuanling together with Hongxian and others to revise and fix them again.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Pei Hongxian, a legal aide under the Prince of Shu, challenged more than forty provisions in the statutes and ordinances, and the emperor ordered Fang Xuanling, Hongxian, and others to revise them again.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等以謂「古者五刑，刖居其一。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others considered that "in antiquity among the five punishments, mutilation occupied one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and his colleagues argued, "In antiquity the five punishments included mutilation as one of them.

sentences.zh: 及肉刑既廢，今以笞、杖、徒、流、死為五刑，而又刖足，是六刑也」。

translations.literal: Once corporal punishments had been abolished, now rod-beating, staff, penal servitude, exile, and death constitute the five punishments, yet to cut off the foot again is six punishments."
translations.idiomatic: After corporal punishments were abolished, the five punishments became rod-beating, staff, servitude, exile, and death. To add foot amputation would make six punishments."

sentences.zh: 於是除斷趾法，為加役流三千里，居作二年。

translations.literal: Thereupon they abolished the law of cutting off the toe and made it augmented penal servitude with exile for three thousand li and labor service for two years.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore abolished toe amputation and substituted augmented penal servitude: exile for three thousand li with two years of labor service.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗覽明堂針灸圖，見人之五藏皆近背，針灸失所，則其害致死，歎曰：「夫箠者，五刑之輕；

translations.literal: Taizong once perused the Hall of Enlightenment acupuncture chart and saw that man's five viscera are all close to the back; if acupuncture missed its place, the harm could cause death. He sighed and said: "Flogging is the lightest of the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once studied the Hall of Enlightenment acupuncture chart and saw that the five viscera lie close to the back; misplaced needling could prove fatal. He sighed and said, "Flogging is the lightest of the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 死者，人之所重。

translations.literal: Death is what men hold weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Death is what people hold most dear.

sentences.zh: 安得犯至輕之刑而或致死？

translations.literal: How can one commit the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?
translations.idiomatic: How can the lightest punishment sometimes bring death?

sentences.zh: 」遂詔罪人無得鞭背。

translations.literal: " He then ordered that criminals must not be flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: " He then decreed that criminals must not be flogged on the back.

sentences.zh: 五年，河內人李好德坐妖言下獄，大理丞張蘊古以為好德病狂瞀，法不當坐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Haode of Henei was imprisoned on a charge of sorcerous speech; the Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Yungu held that Haode suffered from mad delusion and by law should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Li Haode of Henei was imprisoned for sorcerous speech. Assistant Director Zhang Yungu of the Court of Judicial Review argued that Haode was deranged and should not be punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀劾蘊古相州人，好德兄厚德方為相州刺史，故蘊古奏不以實。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, saying he was a man of Xiangzhou; Haode's elder brother Houde was then Prefect of Xiangzhou, and therefore Yungu's memorial did not accord with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, noting that he was from Xiangzhou while Haode's elder brother Houde was then prefect of Xiangzhou, and therefore Yungu had filed a false report.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，遽斬蘊古，既而大悔，因詔「死刑雖令即決，皆三覆奏」。

translations.literal: Taizong was angry and immediately executed Yungu; afterward he greatly regretted it and therefore decreed: "Although capital punishment may be ordered for immediate decision, in all cases there shall be threefold review and memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was enraged and had Yungu executed at once. He soon deeply regretted it and decreed, "Even when capital punishment is ordered for immediate execution, it must receive threefold review and memorial."

sentences.zh: 久之，謂羣臣曰：「死者不可復生。

translations.literal: After a long time he said to the assembled ministers: "The dead cannot be brought back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he told the assembled ministers, "The dead cannot be brought back to life.

sentences.zh: 昔王世充殺鄭頲而猶能悔，近有府史取賕不多，朕殺之，是思之不審也。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Shichong killed Zheng Ting and was still able to repent; recently there was a bureau clerk who took a bribe not large — I killed him; this was failure to deliberate carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong once killed Zheng Ting and still came to regret it. Recently a bureau clerk took only a small bribe, yet I had him killed — I had not thought the matter through.

sentences.zh: 決囚雖三覆奏，而頃刻之間，何暇思慮？

translations.literal: Although the decision of prisoners has threefold review and memorial, within the space of a moment, what leisure is there for reflection?
translations.idiomatic: Even with threefold review, who has time to reflect in the space of a moment?

sentences.zh: 自今宜二日五覆奏。

translations.literal: From now on it is fitting that within two days there be fivefold review and memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth there should be fivefold review over two days.

sentences.zh: 決日，尚食勿進酒肉，教坊太常輟教習，諸州死罪三覆奏，其日亦蔬食，務合禮撤樂、減膳之意。

translations.literal: On the day of decision, the Imperial Provisioners shall not present wine or meat; the Directorate of Education and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices shall suspend instruction and practice; in all prefectures, for capital crimes there shall be threefold review and memorial, and on that day they too shall eat vegetables only, striving to accord with the intent of ritual in withdrawing music and reducing meals.
translations.idiomatic: On execution day the Imperial Provisioners were to serve no wine or meat, the Directorate of Education and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were to suspend performances, and prefectures reviewing capital cases were to observe threefold memorial on that day and eat only vegetables, in keeping with the ritual meaning of withdrawing music and reducing meals.

sentences.zh: 故時律，兄弟分居，蔭不相及，而連坐則俱死。

translations.literal: Under the law of that time, when brothers lived separately their privileges of protection did not extend to one another, yet in collective punishment all were put to death together.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law then in force, brothers who lived apart did not share privileges of official protection, yet collective punishment still required that all be executed together.

sentences.zh: 同州人房彊以弟謀反當從坐，帝因錄囚為之動容，曰：「反逆有二：興師動眾一也，惡言犯法二也。

translations.literal: Fang Qiang of Tongzhou, because his younger brother plotted rebellion, was to be punished by association; the emperor, while reviewing prisoners, was moved on his account and said: "Rebellion has two kinds: raising troops and moving the masses is one; evil speech offending against the law is two.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qiang of Tongzhou was to be punished by association because his younger brother had plotted rebellion. While reviewing prisoners, the emperor was moved and said, "Rebellion takes two forms: raising troops is one, and seditious speech violating the law is the other.

sentences.zh: 輕重固異，而鈞謂之反，連坐皆死，豈定法耶？

translations.literal: Light and heavy are certainly different, yet equally they are called rebellion, and in collective punishment all die — is this a fixed law?
translations.idiomatic: Their gravity clearly differs, yet both are called rebellion and collective punishment brings death to all. Is that a proper fixed law?

sentences.zh: 」玄齡等議曰：「禮，孫為父尸，故祖有蔭孫令，是祖孫重而兄弟輕。

translations.literal: " Xuanling and others deliberated: "By ritual, the grandson stands as the father's corpse; therefore the grandfather has the privilege of protecting the grandson — this shows that grandfather and grandson are weighty while brothers are light.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang Xuanling and his colleagues argued, "By ritual the grandson represents the father's person, which is why the grandfather's privilege extends to the grandson. Grandfather and grandson weigh more heavily than brothers.

sentences.zh: 」於是令：反逆者，祖孫與兄弟緣坐，皆配沒；

translations.literal: " Thereupon an ordinance provided: for those guilty of rebellion, grandfather, grandson, and brothers punished by association were all sentenced to confiscation and exile.
translations.idiomatic: " An ordinance was then issued: in cases of rebellion, grandfathers, grandsons, and brothers punished by association were all sentenced to confiscation and exile.

sentences.zh: 惡言犯法者，兄弟配流而已。

translations.literal: For those whose evil speech offended against the law, brothers were sentenced only to exile.
translations.idiomatic: For seditious speech alone, brothers were sentenced only to exile.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等遂與法司增損隋律，降大辟為流者九十二，流為徒者七十一，以為律；

translations.literal: Xuanling and others then joined the legal offices in adding to and subtracting from the Sui statutes: ninety-two cases in which the great execution was reduced to exile, seventy-one in which exile was reduced to penal servitude — these became the Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and the legal offices then revised the Sui statutes, commuting capital punishment to exile in ninety-two cases and exile to penal servitude in seventy-one, and compiled these as the Statutes.

sentences.zh: 定令一千五百四十六條，以為令；

translations.literal: They fixed one thousand five hundred forty-six articles as the Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed 1,546 articles as the Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 又刪武德以來敕三千餘條為七百條，以為格；

translations.literal: They also culled more than three thousand edicts since Wude down to seven hundred articles as the Administrative Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: They also reduced more than three thousand edicts issued since Wude to seven hundred articles as the Administrative Precedents.

sentences.zh: 又取尚書省列曹及諸寺、監、十六衞計帳以為式。

translations.literal: They further took the account ledgers of the various bureaus of the Department of State Affairs and of the various directorates, supervisorates, and the Sixteen Guards as the Formulae.
translations.idiomatic: They further compiled account ledgers from the Department of State Affairs bureaus, the directorates, supervisorates, and the Sixteen Guards as the Formulae.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣皆有獄，而京兆、河南獄治京師，其諸司有罪及金吾捕者又有大理獄。

translations.literal: All prefectures and counties had prisons; the prisons of Jingzhao and Henan administered the capital; for offenses by the various offices and for those captured by the Gold Crow Guard there was also the Court of Judicial Review prison.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and county had a prison; the Jingzhao and Henan prisons handled the capital. Offenses by government offices and arrests by the Gold Crow Guard were held in the Court of Judicial Review prison.

sentences.zh: 京師之囚，刑部月一奏，御史巡行之。

translations.literal: Prisoners in the capital were reported monthly by the Ministry of Justice, and censors made inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners were reported monthly to the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 每歲立春至秋及大祭祀、致齊，朔望、上下弦、二十四氣、雨及夜未明，假日、斷屠月，皆停死刑。

translations.literal: Each year from the Establishment of Spring to autumn, and on great sacrifices, fasting purification, new and full moon, upper and lower quarter moon, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, rain, and before night was bright, holidays, and months when slaughter was forbidden — on all these capital punishment was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Each year from Establishment of Spring through autumn, and during major sacrifices, fasting periods, new and full moons, quarter moons, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, rain, the hours before dawn, holidays, and slaughter-prohibition months, capital punishment was suspended.

sentences.zh: 京師決死，涖以御史、金吾，在外則上佐，餘皆判官涖之。

translations.literal: When capital punishment was decided in the capital, censors and the Gold Crow Guard attended; outside the capital the chief aide attended; in all other cases judicial reviewers attended.
translations.idiomatic: Capital executions in the capital were supervised by censors and the Gold Crow Guard; in the provinces by the chief aide; elsewhere by judicial reviewers.

sentences.zh: 五品以上罪論死，乘車就刑，大理正涖之，或賜死于家。

translations.literal: For offenses of fifth rank and above punishable by death, they went to execution by carriage; the Director of the Court of Judicial Review attended, or they were granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above who were sentenced to death went to execution by carriage under supervision of the Court of Judicial Review director, or were granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 凡囚已刑，無親屬者，將作給棺，瘞于京城七里外，壙有甎銘，上揭以榜，家人得取以葬。

translations.literal: For all prisoners already punished who had no kin, the Directorate of Palace Buildings supplied coffins; they were buried seven li outside the capital; the tomb chamber had brick inscriptions; a placard was posted above, and the family could take it to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Executed prisoners without kin received coffins from the Directorate of Palace Buildings and were buried seven li outside the capital. Brick inscriptions marked the tomb, a placard was posted above, and relatives could claim the body for burial.

sentences.zh: 諸獄之長官，五日一慮囚。

translations.literal: The chiefs of all prisons reviewed prisoners once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Prison chiefs reviewed cases every five days.

sentences.zh: 夏置漿飲，月一沐之；

translations.literal: In summer they provided drink and gruel; once a month they bathed them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they were given drink and gruel; once a month they were bathed.

sentences.zh: 疾病給醫藥，重者釋械，其家一人入侍，職事散官三品以上，婦女子孫二人入侍。

translations.literal: For illness they supplied medicine; the seriously ill were released from fetters; one person from the family entered to attend them; for active-duty and honorary officials of third rank and above, women, sons, and grandsons — two persons entered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: The sick received medicine; the seriously ill were unfettered. One family member could attend; for active-duty and honorary officials of third rank and above, two female relatives, sons, or grandsons could attend.

sentences.zh: 天下疑獄讞大理寺不能決，尚書省眾議之，錄可為法者送祕書省。

translations.literal: Doubtful cases throughout the realm that the Court of Judicial Review could not decide were jointly deliberated by the Department of State Affairs; those that could serve as law were recorded and sent to the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Cases throughout the realm that the Court of Judicial Review could not decide were deliberated collectively by the Department of State Affairs; precedents suitable as law were recorded and sent to the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 奏報不馳驛。

translations.literal: Memorial reports were not sent by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial reports were not sent by urgent courier relay.

sentences.zh: 經覆而決者，刑部歲以正月遣使巡覆，所至，閱獄囚杻校、糧餉，治不如法者。

translations.literal: For those decided after review, each year in the first month the Ministry of Justice dispatched envoys on inspection tours; wherever they arrived they examined prisoners' fetters and provisions and punished those who managed affairs contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the first month the Ministry of Justice dispatched envoys to review cases decided after appeal. Wherever they went they inspected prisoners' fetters and provisions and punished officials who failed to follow procedure.

sentences.zh: 杻校鉗鎖皆有長短廣狹之制，量囚輕重用之。

translations.literal: Fetters, cangues, shackles, and chains all had regulations of length, shortness, breadth, and narrowness, applied according to the lightness or heaviness of the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Fetters, cangues, shackles, and chains were all regulated in length and width according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 囚二十日一訊，三訊而止，數不過二百。

translations.literal: Prisoners were interrogated once every twenty days; after three interrogations it stopped; the count must not exceed two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were interrogated every twenty days, with interrogation ending after three sessions and the total not exceeding two hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 凡杖，皆長三尺五寸，削去節目。

translations.literal: All staffs were three feet five inches long, with nodes and eyes trimmed away.
translations.idiomatic: All staffs were three feet five inches long, with knots and eyes trimmed away.

sentences.zh: 訊杖，大頭徑三分二釐，小頭二分二釐。

translations.literal: Interrogation staffs: the large end three fen two li in diameter, the small end two fen two li.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation staffs measured three fen two li at the thick end and two fen two li at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 常行杖，大頭二分七釐，小頭一分七釐。

translations.literal: Regular execution staffs: large end two fen seven li, small end one fen seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Regular execution staffs measured two fen seven li at the thick end and one fen seven li at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 笞杖，大頭二分，小頭一分有半。

translations.literal: Rod-beating staffs: large end two fen, small end one fen and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Rod-beating staffs measured two fen at the thick end and one and a half fen at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 死罪校而加杻，官品勳階第七者，鎖禁之。

translations.literal: For capital crimes they wore the cangue with fetters added; for official rank and merit grades of the seventh degree, they were confined with locks.
translations.idiomatic: Capital offenders wore the cangue with added fetters; those of seventh official rank or merit grade were confined with locks.

sentences.zh: 輕罪及十歲以下至八十以上者、廢疾、侏儒、懷姙皆頌繫以待斷。

translations.literal: For light offenses, and for those from under ten years to over eighty, the disabled, dwarfs, and the pregnant — all were detained with loose bonds awaiting decision.
translations.idiomatic: Light offenders, children under ten, the elderly over eighty, the disabled, dwarfs, and pregnant women were all detained without fetters pending final judgment.

sentences.zh: 居作者著鉗若校，京師隸將作，女子隸少府縫作。

translations.literal: Those doing labor service wore manacles or the cangue; in the capital they were assigned to the Director of Palace Construction; women were assigned to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury for needlework.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts at labor wore manacles or the cangue. In the capital they served under the Director of Palace Construction; women were assigned to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury for sewing.

sentences.zh: 旬給假一日，臘、寒食二日，毋出役院。

translations.literal: Every ten-day period one day of leave was granted; on the La festival and Cold Food festival, two days — without leaving the labor compound.
translations.idiomatic: They received one day of leave each ten-day period, and two days at the La and Cold Food festivals — though they were not permitted to leave the labor compound.

sentences.zh: 病者釋鉗校、給假，疾差陪役。

translations.literal: The sick had manacles and cangues removed and were granted leave; when the illness improved they joined labor again.
translations.idiomatic: The sick had their manacles and cangues removed and were granted leave; once recovered, they returned to labor.

sentences.zh: 謀反者男女奴婢沒為官奴婢，隸司農，七十者免之。

translations.literal: For those who plotted rebellion, male and female slaves were confiscated and made government slaves, assigned to the Minister of Agriculture; those seventy and older were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: When someone plotted rebellion, his male and female slaves were confiscated and made government slaves under the Minister of Agriculture; those aged seventy or above were exempted.

sentences.zh: 凡役，男子入于蔬圃，女子入于廚饎。

translations.literal: As a rule for penal service, men entered vegetable gardens; women entered kitchen food preparation.
translations.idiomatic: As a general rule of penal service, men were sent to vegetable gardens and women to kitchen work.

sentences.zh: 流移人在道疾病，婦人免乳，祖父母、父母喪，男女奴婢死，皆給假，授程糧。

translations.literal: Exiles in transit who fell ill on the road, women in nursing exemption, mourning for grandparents or parents, death of male or female slaves — all were granted leave and given journey rations.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles who fell ill on the road, women in postpartum nursing exemption, those mourning grandparents or parents, and the death of male or female slaves — in all such cases leave was granted and journey rations issued.

sentences.zh: 非反逆緣坐，六歲縱之，特流者三歲縱之，有官者得復仕。

translations.literal: Those not implicated by association in treason or rebellion: after six years they were released; those specially exiled, after three years they were released; those who had held office were permitted to resume service.
translations.idiomatic: Those not implicated through collective guilt in treason or rebellion were released after six years; those under special exile after three years; and those who had previously held office were allowed to return to service.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以古者斷獄，訊於三槐、九棘，乃詔：「死罪，中書、門下五品以上及尚書等平議之；

translations.literal: At the beginning, Taizong, because in antiquity criminal cases were tried at the Three Paulownias and Nine Thorn Trees, then decreed: "For capital crimes, officials of fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with the Department of State Affairs and others, shall jointly deliberate them;
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign, Taizong recalled that in antiquity criminal cases were tried at the Three Paulownias and Nine Thorn Trees, and decreed: "In capital cases, officials of fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with the Department of State Affairs and others, shall jointly review the sentence;

sentences.zh: 三品以上犯公罪流，私罪徒，皆不追身。

translations.literal: For those of third rank and above who committed public offenses warranting exile, or private offenses warranting penal servitude, none were to be personally arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of third rank and above guilty of public offenses meriting exile or private offenses meriting penal servitude were not subject to personal arrest.

sentences.zh: 」凡所以纖悉條目，必本於仁恕。

translations.literal: " All the minute and detailed provisions were necessarily rooted in humanity and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: " Every fine provision in the code was grounded in humanity and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 然自張蘊古之死也，法官以失出為誡，有失入者，又不加罪，自是吏法稍密。

translations.literal: Yet from the death of Zhang Yungu onward, judges took erroneous acquittal as a warning; when there was erroneous conviction, no crime was added either — from this the officials' application of law gradually grew stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Zhang Yungu's execution, judges treated erroneous acquittal as the gravest warning, while erroneous conviction went unpunished; from that point the law grew steadily harsher in officials' hands.

sentences.zh: 帝以問大理卿劉德威，對曰：「律，失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the chief of the Court of Judicial Review, Liu Dewei, who replied: "By statute, erroneous conviction reduces punishment by three degrees; erroneous acquittal by five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Liu Dewei, chief of the Court of Judicial Review, who answered: "The statutes reduce punishment by three degrees for erroneous conviction and by five for erroneous acquittal.

sentences.zh: 今失入無辜，而失出為大罪，故吏皆深文。

translations.literal: Now erroneous conviction of the innocent goes unpunished, while erroneous acquittal is treated as a great crime, so officials all apply the law harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now convicting the innocent carries no penalty, while acquitting the guilty is treated as a grave offense — so officials everywhere distort the law to severity.

sentences.zh: 」帝矍然，遂命失出入者皆如律，自此吏亦持平。

translations.literal: " The emperor started in alarm, then ordered that both erroneous conviction and erroneous acquittal be handled according to statute; from this the officials also held the scales even.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was startled, and ordered that both kinds of judicial error be punished as the statutes prescribed; thereafter officials applied the law with greater balance.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔流罪無遠近皆徙邊要州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict declared that exile sentences, regardless of distance, were all to be transferred to strategic border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, an edict ordered that all exiles, whatever the original distance prescribed, were to be sent to strategic border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後犯者寖少。

translations.literal: Afterward offenders gradually became fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the number of offenders gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又徙死罪以實西州，流者戍之，以罪輕重為更限。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, capital convicts were again transferred to populate Western Prefecture; exiles garrisoned it, with terms set according to the lightness or heaviness of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, capital offenders were sent to populate Western Prefecture, with exiles assigned to garrison duty there; terms of service varied according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 廣州都督瓽仁弘嘗率鄉兵二千助高祖起，封長沙郡公。

translations.literal: The military governor of Guangzhou, Qu Renhong, had once led two thousand local troops to help Gaozu rise, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Renhong, military governor of Guangzhou, had once raised two thousand local troops to help Gaozu seize power and was enfeoffed Duke of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 仁弘交通豪酋，納金寶，沒降獠為奴婢，又擅賦夷人。

translations.literal: Renhong consorted with powerful tribal chiefs, accepted gold and jewels, seized surrendered Liao people as slaves, and also levied taxes on the Yi without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: Renhong colluded with powerful tribal chiefs, accepted bribes in gold and jewels, enslaved surrendered tribal peoples, and levied unauthorized taxes on indigenous populations.

sentences.zh: 既還，有舟七十。

translations.literal: When he returned, he had seventy boats.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he came with seventy boats.

sentences.zh: 或告其贓，法當死。

translations.literal: Someone reported his corruption; by law he deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported his corruption, and by law the offense merited death.

sentences.zh: 帝哀其老且有功，因貸為庶人，乃召五品以上，謂曰：「賞罰所以代天行法，今朕寬仁弘死，是自弄法以負天也。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him for his age and past merit, and therefore commuted his sentence to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Reward and punishment exist to execute the law on Heaven's behalf. Now that I have spared Renhong from death, I am tampering with the law and failing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by Renhong's age and former service, commuted his sentence and reduced him to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Reward and punishment exist so that the ruler may execute Heaven's law. By sparing Renhong from death, I have twisted the law and failed Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人臣有過，請罪於君，君有過，宜請罪於天。

translations.literal: When a subject has a fault, he should beg forgiveness from his ruler; when a ruler has a fault, he should beg forgiveness from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When a subject errs, he should beg forgiveness of his ruler; when a ruler errs, he should beg forgiveness of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其令有司設藳席于南郊三日，朕將請罪。

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices set out a straw mat at the southern suburb for three days — I shall beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices prepare a straw mat at the southern suburb for three days, and I shall there beg Heaven's forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 」房玄齡等曰：「寬仁弘不以私而以功，何罪之請？

translations.literal: " Fang Xuanling and others said: "You spared Renhong not from private feeling but because of his merit — what fault is there to beg forgiveness for?
translations.idiomatic: " Fang Xuanling and others said: "Your Majesty spared Renhong not from private favor but for his past service — what offense requires begging forgiveness?

sentences.zh: 」百僚頓首三請，乃止。

translations.literal: " The hundred officials bowed their heads and thrice petitioned him, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled officials kowtowed and thrice entreated him, and at last he desisted.

sentences.zh: 太宗以英武定天下，然其天姿仁恕。

translations.literal: Taizong by martial prowess settled the realm, yet his natural disposition was humane and forbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had conquered the realm through martial prowess, yet his nature was humane and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 初即位，有勸以威刑肅天下者，魏徵以為不可，因為上言王政本於仁恩，所以愛民厚俗之意，太宗欣然納之，遂以寬仁治天下，而於刑法尤慎。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, some urged that stern punishments be used to awe the realm; Wei Zheng held this impossible, and therefore addressed the emperor saying that royal government is rooted in humaneness and grace — the meaning of cherishing the people and enriching custom. Taizong gladly accepted this, and thereafter governed the realm with leniency and humanity, being especially cautious in criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his accession, some urged him to awe the realm with harsh punishments. Wei Zheng objected, arguing that kingship rests on humaneness and grace — the very purpose of cherishing the people and strengthening custom. Taizong gladly accepted this counsel, governed with leniency and mercy, and was especially cautious in matters of criminal law.

sentences.zh: 四年，天下斷死罪二十九人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, throughout the realm death sentences numbered twenty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of his reign, only twenty-nine death sentences were passed empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 六年，親錄囚徒，閔死罪者三百九十人，縱之還家，期以明年秋即刑；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he personally reviewed prisoners, pitied three hundred ninety persons under death sentence, released them to return home, and set the following autumn for execution;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he personally reviewed the prisons, took pity on three hundred ninety condemned prisoners, released them to return home, and appointed the following autumn for their execution;

sentences.zh: 及期，囚皆詣朝堂，無後者，太宗嘉其誠信，悉原之。

translations.literal: When the appointed time came, the prisoners all came to the court hall; none failed to return. Taizong praised their sincerity and trustworthiness, and entirely pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed time came, every prisoner returned to the court; none absconded. Taizong praised their good faith and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 然嘗謂羣臣曰：「吾聞語曰『一歲再赦，好人喑啞』。

translations.literal: Yet he once said to the assembled ministers: "I have heard the saying, 'Pardon twice in one year, and good people fall silent.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet he once told his ministers: "I have heard it said, 'Pardon twice in a single year, and the virtuous will no longer speak out.'

sentences.zh: 吾有天下未嘗數赦者，不欲誘民於幸免也。

translations.literal: Since gaining the realm I have never frequently granted amnesties, because I do not wish to entice the people toward hoping to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne I have never issued frequent amnesties, for I do not wish to teach the people to count on escaping punishment.

sentences.zh: 」自房玄齡等更定律、令、格、式，訖太宗世，用之無所變改。

translations.literal: " From the time Fang Xuanling and others revised the Statutes, Ordinances, Administrative Precedents, and Formulae, through Taizong's reign, they were used without alteration.
translations.idiomatic: " From the revision of the Statutes, Ordinances, Administrative Precedents, and Formulae by Fang Xuanling and others through the end of Taizong's reign, the code remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 高宗初即位，詔律學之士撰律疏。

translations.literal: When Gaozong first took the throne, he decreed that scholars of statutory law compile a commentary on the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Gaozong's reign, he ordered scholars of statutory law to compile a commentary on the penal code.

sentences.zh: 又詔長孫无忌等增損格敕，其曹司常務曰留司格，頒之天下曰散頒格。

translations.literal: He also decreed that Zhangsun Wuji and others add to and reduce administrative edicts; those for the routine duties of the various offices were called Retained Department Precedents; those distributed throughout the realm were called Broadly Distributed Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhangsun Wuji and others to revise administrative edicts: those governing the routine duties of the various offices were called Retained Department Precedents; those issued empire-wide were called Broadly Distributed Precedents.

sentences.zh: 龍朔、儀鳳中，司刑太常伯李敬玄、左僕射劉仁軌相繼又加刊正。

translations.literal: During the Longshuo and Yifeng eras, the Minister of Justice Li Jingxuan and Left Vice Director Liu Ren'gui successively made further revisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo and Yifeng periods, Li Jingxuan, Minister of Justice, and Liu Ren'gui, Left Vice Director, successively undertook further revisions.

sentences.zh: 武后時，內史裴居道、鳳閣侍郎韋方質等又刪武德以後至于垂拱詔敕為新格，藏於有司，曰垂拱留司格。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, Palace Secretary Pei Judao, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Wei Fangzhi, and others further culled edicts and decrees from the Wude era down to Chuigong into new precedents, stored with the relevant offices, called the Chuigong Retained Department Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Pei Judao, Palace Secretary, Wei Fangzhi, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, and others compiled edicts and decrees from the Wude era through Chuigong into new precedents, deposited with the relevant offices as the Chuigong Retained Department Precedents.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，中書令韋安石又續其後至於神龍，為散頒格。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Chief of the Secretariat Wei Anshi continued it thereafter down to Shenlong, making Broadly Distributed Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Wei Anshi, Chief of the Secretariat, continued the compilation through that reign, producing Broadly Distributed Precedents.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，戶部尚書岑羲等又著太極格。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Minister of Revenue Cen Yi and others also compiled the Taizi Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong acceded, Cen Yi, Minister of Revenue, and others compiled the Taizi Precedents.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元三年，黃門監盧懷慎等又著開元格。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong, Supervisor of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaishen and others also compiled the Kaiyuan Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan, Lu Huaishen, Supervisor of the Yellow Gate, and others compiled the Kaiyuan Precedents.

sentences.zh: 至二十五年，中書令李林甫又著新格，凡所損益數千條，明年，吏部尚書宋璟又著後格，皆以開元名書。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fifth year, Chief of the Secretariat Li Linfu again compiled new precedents, adding and removing several thousand articles in all; the next year, Minister of Personnel Song Jing again compiled later precedents — all were titled with the Kaiyuan name.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, Li Linfu, Chief of the Secretariat, compiled new precedents comprising several thousand revisions; the following year Song Jing, Minister of Personnel, compiled supplementary precedents — all bearing the Kaiyuan name.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，又詔刑部尚書蕭炅稍復增損之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, an edict again ordered Minister of Justice Xiao Jiong to make further additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao, an edict ordered Xiao Jiong, Minister of Justice, to revise the code once more.

sentences.zh: 肅宗、代宗無所改造。

translations.literal: Under Suzong and Daizong there were no revisions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong and Daizong the code underwent no further revision.

sentences.zh: 至德宗時，詔中書門下選律學之士，取至德以來制敕奏讞，掇其可為法者藏之，而不名書。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time, an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to select scholars of statutory law, take decrees and memorialized case judgments since the Zhide era, gather what could serve as law and store it, without giving the compilation a formal title.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to select scholars of statutory law, collect decrees and memorialized judgments since the Zhide era, preserve what could serve as law, and leave the compilation untitled.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，刑部侍郎許孟容等刪天寶以後敕為開元格後敕。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time, Vice Minister of Justice Xu Mengrong and others culled edicts after the Tianbao era into Supplementary Edicts to the Kaiyuan Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong, Xu Mengrong, Vice Minister of Justice, and others compiled post-Tianbao edicts into the Supplementary Edicts to the Kaiyuan Precedents.

sentences.zh: 文宗命尚書省郎官各刪本司敕，而丞與侍郎覆視，中書門下參其可否而奏之，為大和格後敕。

translations.literal: Wenzong ordered secretaries of the Department of State Affairs each to cull the edicts of their own bureau; assistants and vice ministers reviewed them, the Secretariat and Chancellery assessed their fitness and memorialized them, making the Supplementary Edicts to the Dahe Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong ordered secretaries in the Department of State Affairs each to compile edicts from their own bureau; assistants and vice ministers reviewed the selections, and the Secretariat and Chancellery evaluated and memorialized them, producing the Supplementary Edicts to the Dahe Precedents.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，刑部侍郎狄兼謩採開元二十六年以後至于開成制敕，刪其繁者，為開成詳定格。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, Vice Minister of Justice Di Jianmo gathered decrees from the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan down to Kaicheng, removed the redundant portions, and made the Detailed Kaicheng Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaicheng, Di Jianmo, Vice Minister of Justice, collected decrees from the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan through Kaicheng, stripped away redundancies, and compiled the Detailed Kaicheng Precedents.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，左衞率府倉曹參軍張戣以刑律分類為門，而附以格敕，為大中刑律統類，詔刑部頒行之。

translations.literal: In Xuanzong's time, Zhang Wei, army store clerk of the Left Guard, classified the penal statutes by category and appended administrative edicts, making the Comprehensive Penal Categories of the Dazhong era; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong, Zhang Wei, army store clerk of the Left Guard, arranged the penal statutes by category with administrative edicts appended, producing the Comprehensive Penal Categories of the Dazhong era, which the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate.

sentences.zh: 此其當世所施行而著見者，其餘有其書而不常行者，不足紀也。

translations.literal: These were what was implemented in their own times and clearly visible; the rest had books but were not regularly enforced — not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: These were the codes actually enforced and clearly attested in their day; others existed in writing but were not regularly applied, and are not worth recording.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「慎乃出令。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Be careful in issuing commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Be careful when issuing commands.

sentences.zh: 」蓋法令在簡，簡則明，行之在久，久則信，而中材之主，庸愚之吏，常莫克守之，而喜為變革。

translations.literal: " For laws and commands lie in brevity — brief, then clear; in enduring execution — long, then trusted. Yet middling rulers and foolish officials commonly cannot uphold this, and delight in making changes.
translations.idiomatic: " Laws succeed through brevity, for brevity brings clarity; through endurance, for endurance brings trust. Yet mediocre rulers and dull officials commonly fail to uphold this, and delight in constant revision.

sentences.zh: 至其繁積，則雖有精明之士不能徧習，而吏得上下以為姦，此刑書之弊也。

translations.literal: When they pile up in complexity, then even keen-minded men cannot fully master them, and officials can manipulate them above and below to commit wrongdoing — this is the defect of books of criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: When codes accumulate into impenetrable bulk, even the sharpest minds cannot master them, and officials manipulate them at every level for private gain — such is the curse of penal law.

sentences.zh: 蓋自高宗以來，其大節鮮可紀，而格令之書，不勝其繁也。

translations.literal: From Gaozong onward, the great principles were rarely worth recording, while the books of precedents and ordinances grew beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong's reign onward, little of grand principle remained worth recording, while the volumes of precedents and ordinances grew beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 高宗既昏懦，而繼以武氏之亂，毒流天下，幾至於亡。

translations.literal: Gaozong was both dim-witted and weak, and the Wu clan's turmoil followed; poison spread through the realm, nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was weak and indecisive, and the Wu clan's reign of terror followed; its poison spread across the realm and nearly brought the dynasty to ruin.

sentences.zh: 自永徽以後，武氏已得志，而刑濫矣。

translations.literal: From the Yonghui era onward, the Wu clan had already gained its aim, and punishments grew excessive.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yonghui era onward, once the Wu clan had gained power, punishment degenerated into abuse.

sentences.zh: 當時大獄，以尚書刑部、御史臺、大理寺雜按，謂之「三司」，而法吏以慘酷為能，至不釋枷而笞棰以死者，皆不禁。

translations.literal: Major cases of the time were jointly investigated by the Ministry of Justice of the Department of State Affairs, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review — called the "Three Offices" — while legal officers took cruelty as merit; even beating prisoners to death without removing the cangue was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases were jointly tried by the Ministry of Justice, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review — the so-called "Three Offices" — while judicial officers treated cruelty as accomplishment; beating prisoners to death without even removing the cangue went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 律有杖百，凡五十九條，犯者或至死而杖未畢，乃詔除其四十九條，然無益也。

translations.literal: The statutes had one hundred blows, altogether fifty-nine articles; offenders sometimes died before the blows were finished. An edict therefore removed forty-nine of the articles — yet to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: The code prescribed one hundred blows in fifty-nine articles, and offenders sometimes died before the full count was delivered. An edict removed forty-nine of those articles — yet it did no good.

sentences.zh: 武后已稱制，懼天下不服，欲制以威，乃修後周告密之法，詔官司受訊，有言密事者，馳驛奏之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu had already assumed regency, feared the realm would not submit, and wished to control it through terror; she therefore restored the Later Zhou system of secret denunciation, decreeing that when offices received interrogations and someone spoke of secret matters, they were to report by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: Once Empress Wu had seized power, fearing the realm would not submit, she sought to rule through terror and revived the Later Zhou system of secret denunciation, decreeing that any secret report heard during an interrogation be sent to her by urgent courier.

sentences.zh: 自徐敬業、越王貞、琅邪王沖等起兵討亂，武氏益恐。

translations.literal: From the time Xu Jingye, the Prince of Yue, Zhen, the Prince of Langye, Chong, and others raised troops to suppress the disorder, the Wu clan grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Jingye, the Prince of Yue, Zhen, the Prince of Langye, Chong, and others took up arms against her, the Wu clan's fear only deepened.

sentences.zh: 乃引酷吏周興、來俊臣輩典大獄，與侯思止、王弘義、郭弘霸、李敬仁、康暐、衞遂忠等集告事數百人，共為羅織，構陷無辜。

translations.literal: She then brought in cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen to manage major cases, and together with Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others gathered several hundred informers, jointly fabricating charges and framing the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: She then put cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen in charge of major cases. Together with Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others, they gathered hundreds of informers, fabricated charges, and framed the innocent.

sentences.zh: 自唐之宗室與朝廷之士，日被告捕，不可勝數，天下之人，為之仄足，如狄仁傑、魏元忠等皆幾不免。

translations.literal: From the Tang imperial clan and court officials, day by day people were denounced and arrested beyond counting; people throughout the realm walked on tiptoe in fear; even such men as Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong nearly could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day members of the imperial clan and court officials were denounced and arrested beyond count; the whole realm lived in dread; even men of the stature of Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 左臺御史周矩上疏曰：「比姦憸告訐，習以為常。

translations.literal: Left Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Recently treacherous and slanderous secret denunciations have become habitual.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Of late, treacherous denunciations and malicious accusations have become routine.

sentences.zh: 推劾之吏，以深刻為功，鑿空爭能，相矜以虐。

translations.literal: Officers conducting investigations take severity as achievement, invent charges to compete in ability, and vie with one another in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating officers treat severity as merit, invent charges to outdo one another, and compete in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 泥耳囊頭，摺脅籤爪，縣髮燻耳，臥鄰穢溺，刻害支體，糜爛獄中，號曰『獄持』；

translations.literal: Plugging the ears and bagging the head, breaking ribs and pricking under the fingernails, hanging by the hair and smoking the ears, making one lie beside filth and urine, carving and harming the limbs until one putrefies in prison — this is called 'Prison Torment';
translations.idiomatic: They stop the ears and hood the head, break ribs and drive splinters under the nails, hang prisoners by the hair and smoke their ears, force them to lie beside filth and ordure, mutilate the body until it rots in the cell — a technique called 'Prison Torment';

sentences.zh: 閉絕食飲，晝夜使不得眠，號曰『宿囚』。

translations.literal: Cutting off food and drink, day and night allowing no sleep — this is called 'Overnight Detention.'
translations.idiomatic: They cut off food and drink and allow no sleep day or night — a technique called 'Sleepless Detention.'

sentences.zh: 殘賊威暴，取快目前。

translations.literal: Cruel, violent, and tyrannical — taking immediate gratification.
translations.idiomatic: They are savage and brutal, gratifying themselves in the moment.

sentences.zh: 被誣者苟求得死，何所不至？

translations.literal: If the falsely accused would accept any death to escape, what would they not do?
translations.idiomatic: When the falsely accused would confess to anything just to die and end their suffering, what limit remains?

sentences.zh: 為國者以仁為宗，以刑為助，周用仁而昌，秦用刑而亡。

translations.literal: One who governs a state takes humaneness as the foundation and punishment as the auxiliary; Zhou used humaneness and flourished; Qin used punishment and perished.
translations.idiomatic: A state should take humaneness as its foundation and punishment as its instrument: Zhou relied on humaneness and prospered; Qin relied on punishment and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 願陛下緩刑用仁，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will relax punishments and employ humaneness — the realm would be greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to soften punishment and govern with humaneness — the realm would be immeasurably blessed!

sentences.zh: 」武后不納。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 麟臺正字陳子昂亦上書切諫，不省。

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang, proofreader of the Lin'tai Pavilion, also submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating; she took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, proofreader of the Lin'tai Pavilion, also submitted an urgent memorial of remonstrance; she ignored it.

sentences.zh: 及周興、來俊臣等誅死，后亦老，其意少衰，而狄仁傑、姚崇、宋璟、王及善相與論垂拱以來酷濫之冤，太后感寤，由是不復殺戮。

translations.literal: When Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were executed, the Empress was also old, and her intent somewhat waned. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together discussed the cruel and excessive wrongs since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved to awakening, and from this no longer carried out slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were put to death, the Empress had also grown old and her zeal somewhat faded. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together reviewed the cruel excesses and wrongful convictions since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved to repentance, and thereafter ceased the killing.

sentences.zh: 然其毒虐所被，自古未之有也。

translations.literal: Yet the poison and cruelty she inflicted had never been seen since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the poison and cruelty of her reign had no precedent in history.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，乃詔法司及推事使敢多作辯狀而加語者，以故入論。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, an edict declared that judicial offices and investigation commissioners who dared to compose excessive written defenses and add incriminating language would be judged under the statute for intentional false conviction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazu, an edict declared that judicial offices and investigation commissioners who fabricated elaborate confessions or inserted incriminating language would be prosecuted for intentional false conviction.

sentences.zh: 中宗、韋后繼以亂敗。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed with disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed, and the court sank again into chaos and ruin.

sentences.zh: 玄宗自初即位，勵精政事，常自選太守、縣令，告戒以言，而良吏布州縣，民獲安樂；

translations.literal: From the beginning of his accession, Xuanzong applied himself diligently to governance, often personally selecting prefects and magistrates and instructing them with admonitions; good officials were spread through the prefectures and counties, and the people obtained peace and contentment;
translations.idiomatic: From the start of his reign Xuanzong applied himself diligently to governance, personally selecting prefects and magistrates and instructing them by edict; capable officials filled the provinces and counties, and the people lived in peace;

sentences.zh: 二十年間，號稱治平，衣食富足，人罕犯法。

translations.literal: Within twenty years, it was called well governed and tranquil; food and clothing were abundant, and people rarely violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty years the age was hailed as one of good order; food and clothing were plentiful, and crime was rare.

sentences.zh: 是歲刑部所斷天下死罪五十八人，往時大理獄，相傳鳥雀不栖，至是有鵲巢其庭樹，羣臣稱賀，以為幾致刑錯。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Justice passed death sentences on fifty-eight persons throughout the realm. In former times at the Court of Judicial Review prison, it was said that birds and sparrows would not perch; now magpies nested in the courtyard trees. The assembled ministers offered congratulations, taking it as nearly achieving a state in which punishments fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Justice condemned only fifty-eight persons to death empire-wide. It was once said that not even birds would perch in the Court of Judicial Review prison; now magpies nested in its courtyard trees. Ministers congratulated the throne, declaring that the age had nearly reached the ideal in which punishments fall unused.

sentences.zh: 然而李林甫用事矣，自來俊臣誅後，至此始復起大獄，以誣陷所殺數十百人，如韋堅、李邕等皆一時名臣，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Yet Li Linfu was already in power; from Lai Junchen's execution until this time major cases were raised again for the first time, and several tens or hundreds were killed through false incrimination — such men as Wei Jian and Li Yong were all eminent ministers of the age, and the realm grieved at the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Linfu was already in power, and for the first time since Lai Junchen's execution major political trials resumed; dozens or hundreds died through fabricated charges. Men such as Wei Jian and Li Yong were among the foremost ministers of the day, and the realm mourned their wrongful deaths.

sentences.zh: 而天子亦自喜邊功，遣將分出以擊蠻夷，兵數大敗，士卒死傷以萬計，國用耗乏，而轉漕輸送，遠近煩費，民力既弊，盜賊起而獄訟繁矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven also delighted in frontier achievements, dispatching generals in separate columns to strike the barbarians; the armies suffered great defeats, soldiers dead and wounded numbering in the tens of thousands; state revenues were exhausted, and transport and grain shipment caused trouble and expense near and far; once the people's strength was spent, bandits rose and lawsuits and litigation multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven also craved frontier glory, dispatching generals on multiple campaigns against southern peoples; the armies suffered repeated defeats, with tens of thousands dead and wounded; state revenues were drained by supply lines stretching across the realm; once the people were exhausted, banditry spread and the courts overflowed with litigation.

sentences.zh: 天子方惻然，詔曰：「徒非重刑，而役者寒暑不釋械繫。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was just then moved with compassion, and decreed: "Penal servitude is not a heavy punishment, yet those at labor are not released from fetters in cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved with compassion, decreed: "Penal servitude is not a grave punishment, yet labor convicts remain shackled through winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 杖，古以代肉刑也，或犯非巨蠧而棰以至死，其皆免，以配諸軍自效。

translations.literal: The staff beating was in antiquity a substitute for mutilation; yet some who had not committed great corruption were beaten to death — let all such be pardoned and assigned to the various armies to redeem themselves through service.
translations.idiomatic: The staff was anciently a substitute for mutilation, yet some offenders of no grave corruption were beaten to death — let all such punishments be remitted, and the offenders assigned to military service to redeem themselves.

sentences.zh: 民年八十以上及重疾有罪，皆勿坐。

translations.literal: Commoners eighty years and above, and those with grave illness who had committed crimes — none were to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners over eighty and the gravely ill who had committed offenses were not to be punished.

sentences.zh: 侍丁犯法，原之俾終養。

translations.literal: Those serving as filial-support laborers who violated the law were pardoned so they might complete their period of care.
translations.idiomatic: Filial-support conscripts who broke the law were pardoned so they could finish caring for their parents.

sentences.zh: 」以此施德其民。

translations.literal: " By this he bestowed virtue upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus he sought to show mercy to the people.

sentences.zh: 然巨盜起，天下被其毒，民莫蒙其賜也。

translations.literal: Yet great bandits arose; the realm suffered their poison, and the people received none of his grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet great bandits ravaged the realm, and the people never tasted his mercy.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，偽官陸大鈞等背賊來歸，及慶緒奔河北，脅從者相率待罪闕下，自大臣陳希烈等合數百人。

translations.literal: In the An-Shi rebellion, the false official Lu Dajun and others deserted the rebels and came over; when Qingxu fled to Hebei, those coerced into following him successively waited to accept guilt beneath the palace gates — from great ministers such as Chen Xilie down, altogether several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: During the An-Shi rebellion, Lu Dajun and other officials who had served the rebel regime defected to the throne; when Shi Qingxu fled to Hebei, those who had followed under duress came in succession to await judgment before the palace gates — from senior ministers such as Chen Xilie on down, several hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫李峴、中丞崔器等為三司使，而肅宗方喜刑名，器亦刻深，乃以河南尹達奚珣等三十九人為重罪，斬于獨柳樹者十一人，珣及韋恆腰斬，陳希烈等賜自盡於獄中者七人，其餘決重杖死者二十一人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor Cui Qi and others were made Three Offices commissioners; Suzong then delighted in criminal law, and Qi was also harsh and severe. Thereupon thirty-nine persons including Daxi Xun, Intendant of Henan, were judged guilty of heavy crimes: eleven were beheaded at the Lone Willow Tree; Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist; seven including Chen Xilie were granted suicide in prison; the rest, twenty-one, were beaten to death with heavy staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor Cui Qi were appointed Three Offices commissioners. Suzong then favored harsh justice, and Cui Qi was himself severe. Thirty-nine men including Daxi Xun, Intendant of Henan, were judged guilty of grave offenses: eleven were beheaded at the Lone Willow Tree; Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist; seven including Chen Xilie were granted suicide in prison; the remaining twenty-one were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 以歲除日行刑，集百官臨視，家屬流竄。

translations.literal: Executions were carried out on New Year's Eve; the hundred officials were assembled to witness; families were exiled and banished.
translations.idiomatic: The executions were carried out on New Year's Eve before an assembly of officials; the condemned men's families were exiled.

sentences.zh: 初，史思明、高秀巖等皆自拔歸命，聞珣等被誅，懼不自安，乃復叛。

translations.literal: At first, Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had all come over of their own accord to submit; hearing that Xun and others had been executed, they feared and were ill at ease, and therefore rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had earlier defected of their own accord; when they learned that Xun and the others had been executed, fearing for their own lives, they rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 而三司用刑連年，流貶相繼。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Three Offices applied punishments year after year, and exile and demotion followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices continued to apply harsh justice year after year, with exile and demotion following one upon another.

sentences.zh: 及王璵為相，請詔三司推覈未已者，一切免之。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu became chief minister, he requested an edict that all cases still under investigation by the Three Offices be entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu became chief minister, he petitioned for an edict pardoning all cases still under investigation by the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 然河北叛人畏誅不降，兵連不解，朝廷屢起大獄。

translations.literal: Yet rebels in Hebei feared execution and would not surrender; warfare continued without end, and the court repeatedly raised major cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebels in Hebei, fearing execution, refused to surrender; the fighting dragged on, and the court repeatedly opened major political trials.

sentences.zh: 肅宗後亦悔，歎曰：「朕為三司所悞。

translations.literal: Suzong afterward also repented, sighing: "I was misled by the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong later repented as well, sighing: "I was led astray by the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 」臨崩，詔天下流人皆釋之。

translations.literal: " On the verge of death, he decreed that all exiles throughout the realm be released.
translations.idiomatic: " On his deathbed he decreed the release of all exiles throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 代宗性仁恕，常以至德以來用刑為戒。

translations.literal: Daizong was by nature humane and forbearing, and often took the use of punishments since the Zhide era as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was humane and forgiving by nature, and constantly held up the excesses of punishment since the Zhide era as a warning.

sentences.zh: 及河、洛平，下詔河北、河南吏民任偽官者，一切不問。

translations.literal: When the He and Luo regions were pacified, he issued an edict that officials and commoners in Hebei and Henan who had served under the false regime were not to be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: Once the He-Luo region was pacified, he decreed that officials and commoners in Hebei and Henan who had served the rebel regime would not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 得史朝義將士妻子四百餘人，皆赦之。

translations.literal: Capturing more than four hundred wives and children of Shi Chaoyi's officers and soldiers, he pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He captured more than four hundred wives and children of Shi Chaoyi's officers and soldiers and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩反，免其家，不緣坐。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, he exempted Huai'en's family from collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, he exempted Huai'en's family from collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 劇賊高玉聚徒南山，啗人數千，後擒獲，會赦，代宗將貸其死，公卿議請為葅醢，帝不從，卒杖殺之。

translations.literal: The ferocious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers in the Southern Mountains and devoured several thousand people; later he was captured. When an amnesty was declared, Daizong was about to spare him from death, but the high officials deliberated and requested that he be made into minced meat; the emperor did not agree, and in the end had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The ferocious bandit Gao Yu gathered a following in the Southern Mountains and devoured thousands of people. After his capture, when an amnesty was declared, Daizong was inclined to spare him, but the high officials urged that he be minced alive. The emperor refused and had him beaten to death instead.

sentences.zh: 諫者常諷帝政寬，故朝廷不肅。

translations.literal: Remonstrators often criticized the emperor's lenient policies, saying that for this reason the court lacked discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators often criticized the emperor's leniency, complaining that the court lacked discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「艱難時無以逮下，顧刑法峻急，有威無恩，朕不忍也。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "In hard times one cannot reach down to the people below; yet if criminal law is harsh and urgent, there is awe but no grace — I cannot bear that.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "In hard times one cannot reach down to the people; yet if the law is harsh and urgent, there is awe but no grace — I cannot bear that."

sentences.zh: 」即位五年，府縣寺獄無重囚。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of his reign, the prisons of the prefectures, counties, and directorates had no serious prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: " Within five years of his accession, the prisons of prefectures, counties, and directorates held no serious offenders.

sentences.zh: 故時，別敕決人捶無數。

translations.literal: In former times, special edicts sentencing people to beating had no limit on the number of blows.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, special edicts ordering beatings imposed no limit on the number of strokes.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔曰：「凡制敕與一頓杖者，其數止四十；

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict declared: "Whenever an ordinance or edict orders a single session of beating, the count shall stop at forty;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, an edict declared, "Whenever an ordinance or edict orders a single session of beating, the count shall not exceed forty strokes;

sentences.zh: 至到與一頓及重杖一頓、痛杖一頓者，皆止六十。
