translations.literal: For those reaching a single session, or a heavy beating in one session, or a painful beating in one session, all shall stop at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: for a single session, a heavy beating in one session, or a painful beating in one session, the count shall not exceed sixty strokes.

sentences.zh: 德宗性猜忌少恩，然用刑無大濫。

translations.literal: Dezong was suspicious and sparing of grace by nature, yet in applying punishments he did not greatly abuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was suspicious and sparing of grace by nature, yet he did not greatly abuse punishment.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎班宏言：「謀反、大逆及叛、惡逆四者，十惡之大也，犯者宜如律。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Ban Hong said: "Plotting rebellion, great treason, rebellion, and wicked treason — these four are among the ten abominations; offenders should be handled according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Ban Hong said, "Plotting rebellion, great treason, rebellion, and wicked treason are among the ten abominations; offenders should be handled according to statute.

sentences.zh: 其餘當斬、絞刑者，決重杖一頓處死，以代極法。

translations.literal: For the rest who merited decapitation or strangulation, one session of heavy staff beating to death should substitute for the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: For all other offenses meriting decapitation or strangulation, one session of heavy staff beating to death should substitute for capital punishment."

sentences.zh: 」故時，死罪皆先決杖，其數或百或六十，於是悉罷之。

translations.literal: " In former times, death sentences were all preceded by staff beating, the count sometimes one hundred or sixty; now all of this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, capital offenders were first beaten, sometimes one hundred or sixty strokes; this practice was now entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 憲宗英果明斷，自即位數誅方鎮，欲治僭叛，一以法度，然於用刑喜寬仁。

translations.literal: Xianzong was heroic, resolute, and clear in judgment; from his accession he repeatedly executed regional commanders, wishing to govern presumption and rebellion entirely by legal standards, yet in applying punishments he favored leniency and humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was heroic, resolute, and clear in judgment. From his accession he repeatedly executed regional commanders, seeking to curb rebellion through law alone, yet in applying punishment he favored leniency and mercy.

sentences.zh: 是時，李吉甫、李絳為相。

translations.literal: At this time Li Jifu and Li Jiang served as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Jifu and Li Jiang served as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 吉甫言：「治天下必任賞罰，陛下頻降赦令，蠲逋負，賑飢民，恩德至矣。

translations.literal: Jifu said: "To govern the realm one must employ reward and punishment; Your Majesty has frequently issued amnesties, remitted arrears, and relieved the hungry — grace has reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu said, "To govern the realm one must employ reward and punishment. Your Majesty has frequently issued amnesties, remitted arrears, and relieved the hungry — Your grace has reached its utmost.

sentences.zh: 然典刑未舉，中外有懈怠心。

translations.literal: Yet canonical punishments have not been carried out, and within and without the court there is a heart of slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet standard punishments have not been enforced, and slackness has spread through the court and the realm."

sentences.zh: 」絳曰：「今天下雖未大治，亦未甚亂，乃古平國用中典之時。

translations.literal: " Jiang said: "Though the realm today is not greatly well governed, it is also not greatly chaotic — this is the time when a peaceful state uses the middle standard of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang replied, "The realm today is not greatly well governed, yet it is not greatly chaotic either — this is the time when a peaceful state applies the middle standard of punishments.

sentences.zh: 自古欲治之君，必先德化，至暴亂之世，始專任刑法。

translations.literal: From antiquity, rulers who wished to govern well must first employ moral transformation; only in ages of violent disorder do they rely solely on criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, rulers who sought good order began with moral transformation; only in ages of violent disorder did they rely solely on criminal law.

sentences.zh: 吉甫之言過矣。

translations.literal: Jifu's words go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu's argument goes too far."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Xianzong considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 司空于頔亦諷帝用刑以收威柄，帝謂宰相曰：「頔懷姦謀，欲朕失人心也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yu Di also insinuated that the emperor should use punishments to recover the handle of authority; the emperor told the chief ministers: "Di harbors treacherous designs and wishes me to lose the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use harsh punishments to recover authority. The emperor told his chief ministers, "Yu Di harbors treacherous designs and wishes me to lose the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 」元和八年，詔：「兩京、關內、河東、河北、淮南、山南東西道死罪十惡、殺人、鑄錢、造印，若彊盜持仗劫京兆界中及它盜贓踰三匹者，論如故。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year of Yuanhe, an edict declared: "In the two capitals, Guannei, Hedong, Hebei, Huainan, and the eastern and western circuits of Shannan, for capital crimes among the ten abominations, murder, coining, seal forging, or armed robbery within the Jingzhao jurisdiction, and other theft of booty exceeding three bolts of silk — the statutes apply as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, an edict declared that in the two capitals, Guannei, Hedong, Hebei, Huainan, and the eastern and western circuits of Shannan, capital crimes among the ten abominations, murder, coining, seal forging, armed robbery within the Jingzhao jurisdiction, and theft of booty exceeding three bolts of silk would be punished as before.

sentences.zh: 其餘死罪皆流天德五城，父祖子孫欲隨者，勿禁。

translations.literal: All other capital crimes were to be exiled to the Five Cities of Tiande; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wished to follow were not to be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: All other capital crimes were commuted to exile at the Five Cities of Tiande; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wished to accompany the exile were not forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」蓋刑者，政之輔也。

translations.literal: " Punishment is the auxiliary of government.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is the auxiliary of government.

sentences.zh: 政得其道，仁義興行，而禮讓成俗，然猶不敢廢刑，所以為民防也，寬之而已。

translations.literal: When government attains the Way, humaneness and righteousness rise and ritual and deference become custom — yet one still dares not abolish punishment, for it serves as a safeguard for the people; one only leniently treats them.
translations.idiomatic: When government attains the Way, humaneness and righteousness flourish and ritual and deference become custom — yet punishment is not abolished, for it safeguards the people; one only moderates its application.

sentences.zh: 今不隆其本、顧風俗謂何而廢常刑，是弛民之禁，啟其姦，由積水而決其防。

translations.literal: Now, without elevating the root and with customs as they are, what does it mean to abolish regular punishments? This relaxes the people's restraints, opens the way to wrongdoing — like storing water and then breaking the dam.
translations.idiomatic: Now, without elevating moral foundations and with customs as they are, what does it mean to abolish regular punishments? This relaxes the people's restraints and opens the way to wrongdoing — like storing water and then breaking the dam.

sentences.zh: 故自玄宗廢徒杖刑，至是又廢死刑，民未知德，而徒以為幸也。

translations.literal: Therefore from the time Xuanzong abolished penal servitude and staff punishments, down to this point capital punishment was again abolished; the people had not yet learned virtue and merely took it as good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Xuanzong abolished penal servitude and staff punishments down to this reign, capital punishment was again effectively abolished; the people had not yet learned virtue and merely counted themselves fortunate.

sentences.zh: 穆宗童昏，然頗知慎刑法，每有司斷大獄，令中書舍人一人參酌而輕重之，號「參酌院」。

translations.literal: Muzong was childish and dull-witted, yet he knew to be cautious in criminal law; whenever the offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to participate in deliberating severity and leniency — this was called the "Participation and Deliberation Office."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was childish and dull-witted, yet he knew to be cautious in criminal law. Whenever the offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to participate in deliberating severity and leniency — the so-called "Participation and Deliberation Office."

sentences.zh: 大理少卿崔𣏌奏曰：「國家法度，高祖、太宗定制二百餘年矣。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Gong memorialized: "The state's laws and institutions — Gaozu and Taizong fixed them for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Cui Gong of the Court of Judicial Review memorialized, "The state's laws and institutions were established by Gaozu and Taizong more than two hundred years ago.

sentences.zh: 周禮正月布刑，張之門閭及都鄙邦國，所以屢丁寧，使四方謹行之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say that in the first month punishments are promulgated, posted at gates and lanes and in capitals and states, so that through repeated admonition all quarters may carefully observe them.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe that in the first month punishments are promulgated and posted at gates and lanes and in capitals and states, so that through repeated admonition all quarters may carefully observe them.

sentences.zh: 大理寺，陛下守法之司也。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 今別設參酌之官，有司定罪，乃議其出入，是與奪繫於人情，而法官不得守其職。

translations.literal: Now to set up separately a participation-and-deliberation office, so that after the relevant office has determined guilt one deliberates increase or decrease — this ties gain and loss to human feeling, and the judge cannot uphold his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Now to establish a separate participation-and-deliberation office, so that after the relevant office has determined guilt another body deliberates increase or decrease — this ties outcomes to human feeling, and judges cannot uphold their duty.

sentences.zh: 昔子路問政，孔子曰：『必也正名乎。

translations.literal: Formerly Zilu asked about government, and Confucius said: 'One must first rectify names.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told Zilu, when he asked about government, 'One must first rectify names.'

sentences.zh: 』臣以為參酌之名不正，宜廢。

translations.literal: ' I consider that the name of participation-and-deliberation is not correct and should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that the name participation-and-deliberation is incorrect and should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」乃罷之。

translations.literal: " It was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 大和六年，興平縣民上官興以醉殺人而逃，聞械其父，乃自歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe, Shangguan Xing, a commoner of Xingping county, killed a man while drunk and fled; hearing that his father had been put in fetters, he returned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dahe, Shangguan Xing of Xingping county killed a man while drunk and fled; when he learned his father had been put in fetters, he surrendered voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰、御史中丞宇文鼎以其就刑免父，請減死。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Intendant Du Cong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding, because he submitted to punishment to spare his father, requested reduction of the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Intendant Du Cong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding, because Xing had surrendered to spare his father, petitioned to reduce the death sentence.

sentences.zh: 詔兩省議，以為殺人者死，百王所守；

translations.literal: An edict ordered deliberation by the two departments, holding that those who kill deserve death — this all kings uphold;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation by the two departments, which held that murderers deserve death — a principle all kings uphold;

sentences.zh: 若許以生，是誘之殺人也。

translations.literal: if one permitted him to live, this would be enticing people to kill.
translations.idiomatic: to spare him would be to entice people to kill.

sentences.zh: 諫官亦以為言。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials also spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials also spoke against leniency.

sentences.zh: 文宗以興免父囚，近於義，杖流靈州，君子以為失刑。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because Xing had spared his father from imprisonment, considered this close to righteousness, and had him beaten and exiled to Lingzhou; gentlemen of the time held that this was a failure of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, moved that Xing had spared his father imprisonment, considered this close to righteousness and had him beaten and exiled to Lingzhou; men of discernment held that justice had been compromised.

sentences.zh: 文宗好治，躬自謹畏，然閹宦肆孽不能制。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved good governance and personally practiced caution and restraint, yet he could not control the wanton crimes of the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved good governance and personally practiced caution and restraint, yet he could not control the eunuchs' wanton crimes.

sentences.zh: 至誅殺大臣，夷滅其族，濫及者不可勝數，心知其冤，為之飲恨流涕，而莫能救止。

translations.literal: When it came to executing and killing great ministers and exterminating their clans, with those implicated beyond counting, he knew in his heart they were wronged, wept tears of bitter resentment for them, yet could not rescue or stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers were executed and their clans exterminated, with countless innocents implicated, he knew in his heart they were wronged, wept in bitter resentment, yet could not rescue them.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁者制亂，而弱者縱之，然則剛彊非不仁，而柔弱者仁之賊也。

translations.literal: The humane govern disorder; the weak indulge it — yet firmness and strength are not inhumaneness, while the weak and soft are the enemies of humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: The humane govern disorder; the weak indulge it — yet firmness is not inhumaneness, while weakness is the enemy of humaneness.

sentences.zh: 武宗用李德裕誅劉稹等，大刑舉矣，而性嚴刻。

translations.literal: Wuzong, using Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; great punishments were carried out, yet his nature was harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong, through Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; great punishments were carried out, yet his nature was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 故時，竊盜無死，所以原民情迫於飢寒也，至是贓滿千錢者死，至宣宗乃罷之。

translations.literal: In former times, petty theft was not capital, in order to excuse the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of booty reaching a thousand cash was capital; only under Xuanzong was this abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In former times petty theft was not capital, to excuse the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of a thousand cash or more was capital; only under Xuanzong was this abolished.

sentences.zh: 而宣宗亦自喜刑名，常曰：「犯我法，雖子弟不宥也。

translations.literal: Xuanzong also delighted in criminal law, often saying: "Those who violate my law — even sons and younger brothers are not spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong also delighted in criminal law, often saying, "Those who violate my law — even kinsmen are not spared."

sentences.zh: 」然少仁恩，唐德自是衰矣。

translations.literal: " Yet he had little humaneness and grace; Tang virtue from this point declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had little humaneness and grace; from this point Tang virtue declined.

sentences.zh: 蓋自高祖、太宗除隋虐亂，治以寬平，民樂其安，重於犯法，致治之美，幾乎三代之盛時。

translations.literal: From Gaozu and Taizong, who removed the Sui's cruel disorder and governed with leniency and peace, the people rejoiced in their security and dreaded offending the law — the beauty of their governance nearly approached the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozu and Taizong, who removed the Sui's cruel disorder and governed with leniency and peace, the people rejoiced in security and dreaded offending the law — their governance nearly approached the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 考其推心惻物，其可謂仁矣！

translations.literal: Considering how they extended their hearts in compassion toward things, they may be called humane!
translations.idiomatic: Considering how they extended their hearts in compassion toward all beneath Heaven, they may truly be called humane!

sentences.zh: 自高宗、武后以來，毒流邦家，唐祚絕而復續。

translations.literal: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the state; the Tang mandate was cut off and then continued.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the state; the Tang mandate was broken and then restored.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初勵精為政，二十年間，刑獄減省，歲斷死罪纔五十八人。

translations.literal: At the beginning Xuanzong applied himself diligently to government; within twenty years, prisons and punishments were reduced, and death sentences in a year amounted to only fifty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning Xuanzong applied himself diligently to government; within twenty years prisons and punishments were reduced, and annual death sentences amounted to only fifty-eight persons.

sentences.zh: 以此見致治雖難，勉之則易，未有為而不至者。

translations.literal: From this one sees that though good governance is difficult, if one strives for it, it is easy — there is nothing attempted that does not reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that though good governance is difficult, if one strives for it, it is easy — nothing attempted fails to reach completion.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，兵革遂興，國家多故，而人主規規，無復太宗之志。

translations.literal: From this time onward, warfare arose in succession, the state had many troubles, and the rulers fussed over small matters without recovering Taizong's ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward warfare arose in succession, the state faced endless troubles, and rulers fussed over small matters without recovering Taizong's ambition.

sentences.zh: 其雖有心於治者，亦不能講考大法，而性有寬猛，凡所更革，一切臨時苟且，或重或輕，徒為繁文，不足以示後世。

translations.literal: Even those who had some heart for governance could not examine and apply the great laws; their natures were lenient or severe by turns, and all their reforms were temporary makeshifts, sometimes heavy, sometimes light — mere redundant text, insufficient to instruct later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Even those with some heart for governance could not examine and apply the great laws; their natures swung between leniency and severity, and all reforms were temporary makeshifts, sometimes heavy, sometimes light — mere redundant text insufficient to instruct later ages.

sentences.zh: 而高祖、太宗之法，僅守而存。

translations.literal: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were only barely preserved and kept in existence.
translations.idiomatic: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were only barely preserved.

sentences.zh: 故自肅宗以來，所可書者幾希矣；

translations.literal: Therefore from Suzong onward, what is worth recording is very little;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from Suzong onward, little is worth recording;

sentences.zh: 懿宗以後，無所稱焉。

translations.literal: from Emperor Yizong onward, there is nothing to praise.
translations.idiomatic: from Emperor Yizong onward, there is nothing to praise.
